Params: The office window framed a thin slice of the sea, where the dying sun spilled scattered gold across the water.
Kalon had been standing at that window for a long while when the sound of the door opening broke the silence behind him.
My assistant said you were waiting for me.
Is it the new stabilizer formula? I remember you wanted to test other isotopes of ytterbium-174.
Ever since you came aboard, the test subjects' survival rate has jumped from under five percent to almost thirty. That's real progress. But we both know it's not enough.
So, any surprises for me today?
The new formula is ready. Phase one results are strong. The associate researcher mentioned...
The associate researcher mentioned that this round's subjects are of exceptional quality. Because you've changed... <color=#ffffffff>suppliers</color>.
Kurono-san only arched an eyebrow, and he then pulled a face that was meant to look apologetic.
The experiments are scaling up. Demand rises with success. I can hardly keep feeding you low-grade material, can I?
But you needn't worry. Whether the subjects are students, vagrants, addicts, or some runaway teenagers, the paperwork all reads the same. Voluntary donors.
And the ones sourced from those illegal gene labs are even better. Superior quality, and practically untraceable.
So this batch is from the gene labs... But all the ones before... were they also—
Kurono-san's expression shifted into a strange kind of pity.
You really do care about this.
You wanted me to find out.
The celebration downstairs is starting soon. Dr. Kalon, you are expected to make an appearance tonight.
The Erhorn family throws one banquet after another. Never any end to them. Even I find them tiresome at this point. But...
Mr. Erhorn won't appreciate you walking in with that look on your face.
Come. Let's go down together. I imagine you have a great many questions for him by now.
The Erhorn family's banquet hall had barely known a quiet night in these years.

The clink of glass and the blur of extravagance mingled into one, topped with a lavish pour of sanctimonious morality. Together they formed the staple dish of the TEC elite's banquet circuit, useless for nourishment but flawless for flaunting taste.
No one need ask if the revelers left hungry. The refined men and women at these galas ate nothing, their mouths too full of ceaseless introductions and gossip to ever touch a plate.
Dr. Kalon, congratulations on your success. The TEC owes you a great debt.

Kalon had long since wearied of the flattery. In earlier days, he would have swept out without a backward glance, leaving Arius' people to tidy up the social mess that a so-called genius was never expected to manage.
Kalon had always misread it as respect from Arius, intelligence defeating money and fame. Now the realization hit cold and hard. He had never been free to leave this circus.
He was no different from that fish skeleton hanging on the wall. Remarkable or peculiar, it was all decoration for the owner's vanity. He was simply a more useful, more advanced piece of decor.
What are you looking at? The fish skeleton?
It was a long, thick white spine, with an enormous tail that swung up and down in a lazy rhythm, driven by the kinetic display.
I've never been able to place what species it was. It's rather beautiful, isn't it? Some kind of shark, perhaps?
Kalon turned to give her an answer, but a cold, pale mechanical hand settled on his shoulder and stopped him cold.
Quite right, Madam Stella. Keen as ever. It is indeed the skeleton of a shark.
I had no idea a shark's tail could be so elegant.
Now you do. Forgive me, madam, but I must borrow our ill-tempered man of science for a moment. You will permit me to spirit him away?
Kalon looked up. Kurono-san stood behind Arius as always, ever obedient, that insufferable smile still fixed on his face.
A moment later, Kalon's terminal lit up.
It seems Miss Cordelia's condition has deteriorated again.
Kalon drew a deep breath and fell into step behind them.
But before they stepped into the private lounge, Arius swept a cold glance over Kurono-san.
The man caught the signal at once, stopping in his tracks and gesturing them inside.
Then he spoke with a lowered voice.
Dr. Kalon, I wonder if it's ever crossed your mind. Those subjects, back when they were still breathing... received the exact same experimental modifications as Miss Cordelia.
I've already had your latest stabilizer sent to the hospital. Let's hope it brings good news.
Poor Miss Cordelia. We really must accelerate the progress, don't you agree?
Before the door swung shut, that smile crept back onto his face.
The curve of his lips was warm and genial, a flawless mask.
Once the door clicked shut, every sound from the outside world dropped away.
Kurono-san told me you've figured things out?
You really should have pretended otherwise. I've always taken great care to protect you from unpleasant information.
I thought we had an understanding.
Kalon had no interest in any of it.
Cordelia's modification procedure... why did it result in a medical accident?
Arius turned around, one eyebrow arched.
It was never meant to save her. That's why the surgical procedures were so aggressive.
That's why the side effects never stopped, why she's been in pain every day since.
When she was trapped underground with that sleeping pod, I confess it did give me pause. You have no idea... how valuable that pod was.
But then, using a direct Erhorn bloodline as a test subject might produce far more precise results... Letting her go seemed the optimal course of action.
And really, even with how poorly her body responded to the modifications, the lab never treated her as disposable material.
I've always looked after her. Every treatment she received came directly from your latest research.
She has lived her entire life as a noble young lady of the Erhorn family. Never once has she had to lower her head.
I've done my very best for her, Professor Kalon.
He selected a bottle from the wine rack, his voice laced with something almost indulgent.
Kurono-san is a man who bets on every horse at the track. Are you truly prepared to abandon our great cause over the provocations of someone like him?
Have a glass of wine and go back to the lab. What do you say?
Kurono-san? You think this is about him? Illegal gene modifications, trafficking in human subjects... Arius, do you have any idea what your own laboratory has been doing?
Illegal gene labs. Human subjects. This is what's shaken you so badly? I told you from the very start that I would give you my full support.
The Ethics Committee, and even Dominik himself... None of them can touch you while I stand behind you.
What I meant by that was simple: you are free from every ethical restraint, every social constraint. You are free to devote yourself, purely and absolutely... to truth.
I never asked for that kind of support.
Don't dress up your crimes as generosity toward me. I will not be part of experiments that cross every line, and I will not continue them.
Arius poured a glass of wine with unhurried ease and slid it across the table toward Kalon.
Is that so? You didn't know, therefore you are blameless. You didn't approve, therefore every experiment you conducted with those materials can be simply erased.
Tell me, Dr. Kalon. Did you ever lack for funding? Did a piece of equipment ever arrive late?
Every specimen, every sample you requested. It appeared on your bench by morning without exception. And you—only now, after all this time—you think to ask where it all came from?
The color drained from Kalon's face.
...I won't run from what I've done. I will face whatever judgment the law and morality demand.

I'm not foolish enough to leave evidence lying around, Doctor. Rest assured, I've preserved your good name. Legally, you are entirely innocent. Kurono has borne the full weight of it for the Erhorn family.
And morality? Morality is like the law, nothing more than a set of rules concocted by humanity's sentimental little minds so the weak can pretend they have dignity.
Our society sacrifices the strong so the weak may survive. So in exchange, what is the harm in science doing the same, sacrificing a few to propel all of humanity forward?
Dr. Kalon, humans die. But truth is immortal. Truth does not care where it comes from. Truth is simply the objective result.
In no time at all, your work has already outpaced everything that pack of useless primates in the lab achieved in ten years.
Compassion? Morality... Set aside these imaginary concepts and ask yourself: how far could you truly go?
A self-deprecating smile flickered across Kalon's face.
A molecular structure does not lose its efficacy because it was extracted from a corpse. An experimental result does not change its nature based on how it was achieved.
I have to admit it. There is no inherent moral link between means and ends.
Kalon shook his head and took a step back.
But I cannot embrace that logic with a clear conscience, and I don't need that kind of absolution... the kind that lets me walk away without responsibility.
I will carry this guilt. That is the fundamental difference between us. I am human... Just like the materials you speak of. We share the same flesh. The same soul.
Without human warmth, truth means nothing.
Besides, do you even care about truth at all?
That skeleton in the banquet hall is a marlin. The one we caught together, on our last trip out to sea.
Oh? Is that what it was?
I no longer care for it being a marlin. A shark, however... that would be a much better answer.
He dropped all pretense and showed the smile of a monster.
Kalon, what matters is not what something originally was, but that I define what it is.
I understand why you came here tonight. And this is my final answer.
In science, you are a genius. But in your understanding of human nature, you remain as naive as a child.
Don't pretend your hands are clean, Dr. Kalon. You've only just opened your eyes and noticed the blood.
He watched Kalon leave, then emptied his glass into the plant on the table.
...One after another. So naive it's almost endearing.
Kalon pushed open the banquet hall doors, and the noise and light crashed over him all at once. Eager smiles turned in his direction. Glasses were raised in his honor.
He has never felt so cold.
His terminal buzzed quietly in his pocket.
Ms. Erhorn is out of danger.
<color=#ffffffff><size=40>The latest stabilizer worked really well.\nThe rejection response has stopped.\nYou've saved her again, Dr. Kalon.</size></color>
The latest stabilizer worked really well. The rejection response has stopped. You've saved her again, Dr. Kalon.
She's the one who saved me.
If there was anything in all this wickedness that could still stir his courage, it was the fact that Cordelia was still alive.
The sea wind carried away sunrise after sunrise, sunset after sunset.

Under tight watch ever since, Kalon no longer took part in the experiments. But he began to search with desperate focus for a way to free Cordelia from her hospital bed, to restore her to something like a normal life.
After this round of modification, you should be able to live almost like anyone else... But the rejection stopping doesn't mean your body has fully integrated the parts.
You'll be dealing with the side effects of the experiments for the rest of your life.
None of this should have happened to you...
It's already more than I thought I'd get. You told me yourself, living is what matters the most.
Professor, when everyone else stopped trying, you didn't. You chose me. You saved my life.
So stop blaming yourself. I'm alive. That's enough for me to be grateful.
Kalon lowered his head, shame and exhaustion bearing down on him like a weight he could no longer carry.
You know, you really shouldn't look this miserable in front of a patient.
The girl held out a tiny "star" to him.

From your last lesson. If you apply a controlled electrical signal to an entangled crystal, the piezoelectric effect alters its stress state. That changes the decoherence efficiency, and the amplitude of the characteristic peak fluctuates as a result.
So, I used strong and weak signal levels to represent 1s and 0s. This translator just reads the amplitude curve and converts it into a binary stream.
So? Any engineering potential in here?
If I recall correctly... the lesson was about maintaining signal purity in every source within the device to prevent interference. Did that part of the lecture escape you entirely...?
What I see is a lot of potential for troublemaking.
The smile on Cordelia's face faltered for a heartbeat. Kalon, whose words had been meant lightly, recognized his mistake immediately.
With the experiment's truth laid bare, they could no longer look upon the technology that had saved Cordelia without seeing its darkness.
Every day they lived now was a day borrowed against a terrible debt.
You're right. After all... I am an Erhorn.
Kalon cut her off without a moment's pause. He picked up her translator and examined it closely, turning it over in his hands.
In theory, the characteristic peak should also produce a very faint disturbance in the surrounding physical field...
Let me think about this. If I can design a transducer to capture those microscopic disturbances and amplify them into mechanical vibrations in the audible range...
Your translator won't just render text anymore. It'll have a voice... It won't be simple, but... it's worth attempting.
I have a gift for you too.
A mechanical potted plant wobbled unsteadily into the air.
You can grow real plants in it if you like. Or, if you don't have much of a green thumb, the biosphere has a whole collection of projections to choose from.
You can't let them operate on you anymore. Ytterbium-174X3 stabilized your condition, yes, but Ytterbium-174 itself is volatile, and as its isotope, X3 is hardly tame.
Its mechanism is comparable to radiation. The modifications already made to your body... I can't reverse them. But this stabilization program will keep the pain to a minimum.
I'm installing it in this plant. That way, even after you leave, even without regular maintenance, you'll still be able to function.
Be careful. More careful than you've ever been. Wait for the right moment, and then get out. Escape all of this.
Life matters, Cordelia. Every single life matters... That's the reason I saved you. That's the reason we met. And that's the reason we carry this guilt for the innocent.
Take root, grow, and wait for the day you bloom.
It was the final conversation they ever had in person.
On the eve of that horrifying purge, after paying a price that nearly cost him half his life, Kalon finally escaped the Transatlantic Economic Community with the aid of the Science Council.
Years later, the shadow of the Erhorn name once again stretches across these waters.
In all the generations of the Erhorn family... not a single one has ever warranted a second look from me.
But you, Karenina. You are something else entirely. Far more exquisite than I ever dared to imagine...
The colossal whale cruises through the deep, its body a patchwork of ocean waste and Corrupted, the jagged contour made more hideous by the Red Tide.
A single scaleless fish slips soundlessly to Karenina's side.
Then, as though obeying some unheard signal, the entire school follows the leader's path and closes in around her within a heartbeat.
I've reconsidered... Stand with me, Karenina. What do you say?

You have never glimpsed the power that slumbers in the depths of your own M.I.N.D... The new life the Erhorn family granted you was meant to remake you entirely. To raise you to a height where you might look down upon the world as gods do...
And yet all these years, how has Babylonia spent that gift?
And now? One small provocation, and they could not wait to toss you out onto this sea like a piece they were willing to lose.
But it doesn't have to be that way... All you need to do is stand beside me.

We would answer to no one. We would open the "Gateway" with our own hands and rewrite the rules of this world as they were always meant to be written. This broken, putrid, irredeemable world—we could reshape it into something truly beautiful...
Power. Knowledge. A span of life that stretches toward forever. Anything you can imagine, anything you desire... it would all be yours.
Don't mistake me for your enemy. We are already in the same vessel, you and I, steering the only ark that sails against an unbeatable tide.
Welcome to the right side of history.
Take your garbage philosophy and choke on it! I don't want a single thing you're offering!
She tears herself free from the grasping swarm of fish. In the same moment, her auditory module catches a low hum.
Tch... You still believe you have options?
From the moment you set foot in these waters, your M.I.N.D. was already cycling back into the growth phase of a test subject.
The hell is that supposed to mean?!
What did you imagine those whale calls were? A lullaby to soothe you to sleep? They were a reveille, a call to wake what has always been dormant inside you.
The anomalous crystals laced into those repeaters contain an isotope of Ytterbium-174, discovered by none other than your own grandfather, Kalon.
It functions as a reducing agent. Within its "radiation" field, your M.I.N.D. will revert slowly... back into what it was originally designed to be: the perfect vessel.
Each repeater you tear out, modify, or swap pushes your M.I.N.D. closer to its original state. The state of a perfect subject.
Of course... during the procedure, you may experience some "minor" discomfort.
Karenina's heart hammers in her chest. Perhaps it is the anchor drawing near.
Or perhaps it is the truth now spilling from Arius' mouth.
Continue replacing the repeaters, and the part of you called Karenina will be erased entirely. You will become a part of me.
Abandon the mission, and every scrap of data flooding through those cables will feed the Sefirah I carry, without end.
Do you see it now, Karenina? As long as you stand against me, you lose no matter which path you choose. That is the curse fate has written for you.
But stand beside me, and you share that victory.
Consider that a promise from a "god."
...You vile piece of work. You actually stand there and call yourself a god.
A blade of light tears through the sea like a bolt of lightning, water shuddering in its wake.
Before the self-proclaimed god can speak again, her anchor, sent by the commandant, reaches her first.
She seizes her weapon and holds it tight.
Karenina lifts her head. Her gaze cuts through the swarming fish and the churning deep, straight to the vast, dark silhouette looming before her.
If you were so sure of winning, you wouldn't be here trying to stop me.
A scornful smile flashes across the girl's face.
Arius Erhorn. You're just a man who doesn't even understand himself.
I'm going to replace every single one of those repeaters. Nothing you say changes that.
And as for you and that Sefirah of yours, someone will come to stop you. Always.
You stand alone. But the people standing with me... they are the ones I treasure most in this world.
Faces flicker through Karenina's M.I.N.D., vivid and alive.
Soldiers, some familiar, some buried in memory.
Those who remained in the past forever.
Those who still fight at her side.
Those who are waiting somewhere for her to come back.
All the scattered, burning moments of her past swell like sparks caught in a wind.
If this world had only one of my comrades left in it, that one person would still come to stop you.
Take your fate and your promise, and go to hell!
Her frame strains against the weight of the sea as she lifts the anchor high.
Because even if I'm going down... I am dragging you with me!
The anchor splits the crushing pressure of the Red Tide and slams down with brutal force.

The giant whale, that grotesque assembly of ocean waste and fish, unleashes a scream of pure agony. The wound the anchor leaves spreads along its spine like a crack through stone. Ink-thick Red Tide gushes from the fissure, and the false leviathan crumples apart in an instant.
If you refuse to join me as an equal, then you may return to the fate you were always meant for. A stepping stone beneath my ascent to the throne.
The Red Tide clings to her like hot tar, and every inch forward demands that she rip through another viscous membrane.
Her arms drive upward against the crushing deep. Before the raw power of nature, she is nothing but a thin, stubborn blade, and yet she dares to carve the sea's belly open from within.

The shattered leviathan wails its final, mournful cry. Karenina's consciousness starts to slip and blur. The whole ocean drags at her, pulling her down toward that despair, thicker and heavier than blood.
She fights to raise her head and stares into the ink-dark red pressing down from above. The crimson sea closes in around her like an impossible cage, like a fate she cannot escape.

Her grandfather's smile. The look in Wise's eyes. The book page flipped by Bianca. The mischievous grin of Teddy. The commandant's back, steady and sure. These are the finest things she has ever been given.
If you continue replacing the repeaters, everything that makes you Karenina will be stripped away from you.
Do you understand what that means?
All the things that made Karenina who she is, the most essential pieces of her, drift away with the current.
Her fingers close on water that slips away without fail.

Then the noise, her constant shadow, comes to her once more. Perhaps it is because she is utterly alone, trapped beneath the sea, that it holds her now with an intimacy it has never shown before and pulls her back into focus.

A sound like something dying pulses through her consciousness, again and again. It is a deep and hollow loneliness, a pain that surges like the ocean, wave after wave, trying to bury her in the abyss.
Yet from this pain, from this solitude, a desperate stubbornness always finds a way to grow.
(I'm not the kind of idiot... who just rolls over and quits...)
Suddenly, a sharp light rips through the heavy fog. A steady, unwavering warmth floods her thoughts and fills her M.I.N.D. completely, illuminating everything.
That M.I.N.D. connection, steady as an anchor chain, seizes hold of her once more.
It's faint and far away. It sounds like dry stardust colliding in the wind, or the tiny blooms of baby's breath swaying on their stems.
Stars... that's the sound of stars...
The sound, fine as stardust, spreads in ripples through the dark. The steady, warm connection sinks into her consciousness like an anchor lowered from the sea's surface.
Within that quiet embrace, distant memories rise. Fragments pressed down for years beneath her subconscious float up like bubbles, one by one.
Maybe she'll hate drawing and love singing instead. Just anything but engineering.
Someone held her in their arms, soothing her with gentle pats and a soft, humming lullaby.

A pretty face is just wrapping. Talent is a walking stick. Nice to have, but not what gets you up the mountain. If I could give you anything, I'd give you courage that never wavers and a soul that shines bright.
Someone touched her cheek with gentle fingers. Someone leaned down and shielded her from the ocean's biting wind.
(Is that you... Mom... Was I ever a child precious to someone...)
The deck tilted sharply beneath her. The sound of the hull tearing apart mingled with the howl of the waves.
Someone crashed hard to the deck, then fought their way upright again. Cradled in their arms, she could only make out a blurred patch of sky through the violent shaking.
I'm giving you all my luck, my baby.
A light, fleeting kiss was pressed against her cheek. Then someone threw her upward, and the sudden weightlessness felt like a desperate, terrifying escape.
Don't become whatever fate wants you to be.
Her shattered memories spill like an overturned palette, their bright colors driving away the vicious, thick crimson tide pressing in around her.
Her grandfather's face sharpens into perfect clarity.
Karenina, do you know where the universe and all the stars come from?
The tenderness in his features remains unchanged. It carries her back to a time when she was still just a little girl.
A theory says that the universe was just a lifeless singularity before it exploded and created everything beautiful!
It was an explosion that created everything beautiful.
It is not the curse of fate, but her answer to it. She will break herself so that something beautiful can come into being.
I will... always believe in hope. And if there's no hope to be found... then I'll make my own.
A choked cry tears from her throat, overlaid with the thrum of her frame. Every inch of her skin and every joint screams with effort and fury.
Even in a dead end she knows is hopeless, she will not bow to fate. She will make her last desperate stand like a fool.
Her shoulders tear through the surface.
She lifts her head and drinks in the air, real air, greedy and deep.
Seawater streams from her hair and splits into a thousand rivulets over her shoulder blades. She rises from the waves and stands tall on her surfboard.
The Mid-Atlantic Ridge stretches on for thousands of miles. Somewhere along that path, the cursed repeaters wait for her to finish what she came to do.
Odin knew long ago how the twilight of the gods would fall, fate repeating in an endless loop no one can escape.
Yet neither god nor mortal has ever walked quietly into the waves.
She will offer up everything she holds most precious to trade for something called hope, a hope that belongs to this world.
She has climbed back from the abyss only to meet her end.
The boundless sea spreads before her, vast and open like Karenina's heart.
And that open heart is connected now to the one she trusts most.
Commandant, in all those horrors you've survived, did you ever face a moment where every road was a dead end?
If failure is all that's waiting, no matter which way you turn... then what do you do?
Being destroyed never means being defeated.
That's from Larsen's story, isn't it... I still don't really get it.
Giving up and doing nothing—that's the only real failure.
Some hear the howl of fate and choose another road. Some glimpse its shadow stretching across their path and turn away.
Never look it in the face, and fate's spear will never pierce your heart.
Yet those who refuse to bow to fate always stand closer to ruin than most.
But it is this very defiance, this endless raging against the inevitable, that proves they have never surrendered.
Giving up and doing nothing—that's the only real failure... I see.
Those golden eyes lock onto the shadows jutting from the sea like rows of fangs. She listens to the wind shrieking through the battered hulls.
She will find the path that leads to a fight with fate itself.
She will find the path that leads to a fight with fate itself.
She will prove what ruin and failure truly mean.
She will prove what ruin and failure truly mean.
I'm not taking another road. I'll... chart us a course straight through.
I'm going to do something about this, Commandant. So don't you dare underestimate me.
I'll keep watch over your ship like you're still aboard.
She plunges into the deep water. She hurls herself into fate.
(Maintain the M.I.N.D. connection and keep it steady)
Both of you push past the unsettling pain and let the steady anchor drop deep into her heart.
In the profound and silent water, she sees another pair of eyes following her own, another heartbeat pressing close to hers.
She searches through the churning Red Tide for the right path, the way an engineer explores the grain of an unfamiliar material, cutting a navigable vein from the unknown.
A gnawing pain shoots along her nerves and reverberates through her frame. She is impossibly small against the vastness of the ocean, and yet the agony inside her feels immense.
The other end of the M.I.N.D. connection dims. You track her "trace" the way one might chase a falling star, following the faint trail of its descent.
She has gone deeper now, farther than ever before.
Tch. I knew you'd forget everything I just said. What did I tell you?
That's right. Now watch me work.
The sting across Karenina's skin slowly ebbs away. The thick rot in the air thins alongside it, and every sense that binds her to the world grows faint and far.
Touching the repeaters numbs all five senses. Memory, feeling, pain, they all soften into a blur. And yet, strangely, it suits this moment exactly.
Forget the pain, Karenina. Forget the fear.
Now, through this very dulling that is meant to undo her, she crests the towering waves once more, a miracle against the odds.
In the dim, blurred world beneath the surface, her voice cuts like a tiny blade slicing through the ocean's flesh. Small, but sharp beyond measure.
I want to chart a course for this ship.
I want to do something for this world.
I want to be a name that shines. The kind of name that belongs beside yours.
Fire ruptures the darkness, blazing across the endless water in a sudden, violent flash.
Of course you do. You can see everything she sees.

The ocean ahead darkens as the Punishing Virus concentration rises. Karenina does not slow. She calculates the timing, the distance, and the radius of each blast, and throws miniature charges one after another into the calculated positions behind her.
Fire threads into fire, tracing a line over the waves.
Explosion piles on explosion, each flame feeding the next. Karenina's surfboard streaks across the water, and the dark blue sea catches light behind her, flaring into a long burning trail.
The flames become blazing markers, carving a fiery route of fire across the Red Tide.
The cascading echoes of the fire that engulfs the ocean are her scream, meeting fate's roar with her own.
The flames throw red and trembling light across the water. Her silhouette cuts through the glow, striking back against the shadow fate has laid across her path.
You follow her gaze across the sea ignited by countless flames, tracing the course of life. The broken half of the ship drives forward, pushing out of the Red Tide.
We advance through the wounds fate has dealt us. Those wounds are the road we tore open for ourselves.
We advance through the wounds fate has dealt us. Those wounds are the road we tore open for ourselves.
Through the shared sight, everything in her world is so vivid. Her voice, her heart, all of it becomes impossibly clear.

Deep inside the part of the M.I.N.D. she cannot share, Karenina finds herself lost. She finally understands what she has lost. Not just the sense of touch that once warned her of pain and kept her from harm, but the joy that should be flooding her right now.
And still, she makes her voice sound so fiercely alive.
This... is the course for every life!
The warmth of the connection between them feels so vivid, so achingly real, that it makes her believe no hardship could ever stop her.
Yet she realizes at the same moment that when the day arrives, even this thin thread tying her to the commandant will be taken by fate.
Behind her, the fire rages. Around her, the waves heave. And in this single, transient breath, she kindles a path made of light.
